The skeleton cycles identify canonically with wedge^(k-1)U. A private face of every attached k-simplex gives a signed unit minor, so its oriented boundary map is primitive and injective integrally. The quotient is free. Integral equivariant combinatorial Alexander duality gives the sign twist and dual; universal coefficients remove hidden torsion. originality.rationale: The accepted claim is the natural integral Aut(G)-lattice as an explicit primitive quotient of wedge^(k-1) of the vertex augmentation lattice, dualized with the vertex orientation character. Full inspection identified decisive antecedents for every non-novel component: the 2026 high-girth result already proves the wedge homotopy type, free ranks and private facet; the 2024 primary formula (15) already covers the rational virtual character. Neither inspected source gives the stated integral lattice presentation or modular representations, which cannot be reconstructed uniquely from rational characters or homology ranks. Searches for this exact integral presentation, augmentation wedge, modular equivalences and broader coverage did not identify an identical result. This is best-knowledge originality, not a proof of priority.

value.rationale: The natural ZAut(G) module is given by a uniform exact quotient presentation for all girth>=k+2 graphs and all k>=4 in scope. Integral actions are not specified by rational characters or sphere ranks, especially in modular characteristic. Saturated signed boundary relations provide a reproducible, computation-ready full integral classification without requiring graph-specific homology computations; it describes which connected induced trees impose relations. This is a motivated structural representation problem, not a new claim about the already known wedge count or virtual rational traces.
